content: Fexinidazole is indicated for the treatment of African trypanosomiasis (HAT or sleeping sickness) caused by Trypanosoma brucei gambiense. It is effective in both stage 1 (hemolymphatic) and stage 2 (meningoencephalitic) HAT. The drug is approved for use in children aged 6 years or older who weigh at least 20 kg. However, its safety and efficacy in children under 6 years of age have not been established. Fexinidazole interacts with various drugs by inhibiting or inducing hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4, CYP1A2, CYP2C19, and CYP2B6. These interactions can lead to increased or decreased plasma concentrations of co-administered drugs, potentially resulting in adverse effects or reduced efficacy. Below are specific drug interactions and recommendations: 1. Fezolinetant: Fexinidazole increases fezolinetant levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 2. Lonafarnib: Fexinidazole increases lonafarnib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 3. Mavacamten: Fexinidazole increases mavacamten levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism, which may lead to heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 4. Abemaciclib: Fexinidazole increases abemaciclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 5. Acalabrutinib: Fexinidazole increases acalabrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Ado-trastuzumab emtansine: Fexinidazole increases ado-trastuzumab emtansine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 7. Albuterol: Both fexinidazole and albuterol prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 8. Alfentanil: Fexinidazole increases alfentanil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Alfuzosin: Fexinidazole increases alfuzosin levels and prolongs the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 10. Alpelisib: Fexinidazole increases alpelisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Amiodarone: Both fexinidazole and amiodarone prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 13. Amisulpride: Both fexinidazole and amisulpride prolong the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administered. 14. Amitriptyline: Both fexinidazole and amitriptyline prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 15. Amlodipine: Fexinidazole increases amlodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 16. Amobarbital: Amobarbital increases fexinidazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 17. Amoxapine: Both fexinidazole and amoxapine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Anagrelide: Both fexinidazole and anagrelide prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 19. Apalutamide: Fexinidazole increases apalutamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 20. Artemether/lumefantrine: Fexinidazole increases artemether/lumefantrine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 27. Asenapine: Both fexinidazole and asenapine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 28. Atenolol: Fexinidazole may synergistically increase the effects of atenolol, leading to bradycardia. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 30. Atomoxetine: Both fexinidazole and atomoxetine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 31. Avatrombopag: Fexinidazole increases avatrombopag levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 35. Axicabtagene ciloleucel: Fexinidazole may increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 36. Axitinib: Fexinidazole increases axitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 37. Azithromycin: Both fexinidazole and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 38. Bedaquiline: Fexinidazole increases bedaquiline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 39. Belumosudil: Fexinidazole increases belumosudil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 40. Belzutifan: Belzutifan decreases fexinidazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when fexinidazole is co-administered with other medications.
